gen-dafont-brusher-work-sans: Work Sans stands tall and plain beneath Brusher's heavy, calligraphic strokes, its high mean line and unpinched c tips giving the script room to flourish. Try nothing too small up top.
gen-dafont-capture-it-fs-gambetta: Gambetta reads like a bookish text serif, its stroke weight shifting noticeably without ever getting dramatic. And Capture It towers above it, urban and nearly sealed, with no thick-thin flicker to soften it.
gen-dafont-capture-it-lora: Capture It towers with a huge x-height and letters that feel nearly sealed shut. But Lora, a text serif with a broad, welcoming c, opens everything back up and lets the lowercase breathe.
gen-dafont-capture-it-noto-serif: Capture It has a towering x-height and curves with no stress at all. Noto Serif does the gentler work, its moderate thick and thin cadence making paragraphs easy to follow while the heading stays blunt and urban.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-fs-gambetta: Capture Smallz has big-bodied lowercase that looks raw and tactical. Gambetta, a text serif with wide channels into each counter, would feel the strain if the heading went small or the body went large.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-lora: Raw, chunky and tactical, those big lowercase shapes announce Capture Smallz at once. Lora, a text serif with modest hairline thinning and a welcoming c, gives that bluntness a literary counterweight.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-noto-serif: Noto Serif brings gently modulated strokes with no sharp hairlines, a classic serif texture beside the big-bodied, raw lowercase of Capture Smallz. Pages of it would read smoothly and quietly.
gen-dafont-cheri-bitter: Cheri is a soft, inviting script with no hairlines at all. Its sturdy tall lowercase handles the friendly greeting, while Bitter, a slab-serif with a large lowercase eye and a visible gap in each s, handles the grounded, dependable reading.
gen-dafont-cheri-fs-merriweather-sans: Cheri's calligraphic hand carries curves as thick as its stems, so every word looks sturdy and large. Merriweather Sans follows with tall lowercase and a clearly open e, keeping the page easy to follow.
gen-dafont-cheri-instrument-sans: Instrument Sans keeps its stroke weight constant, with c ends pointing apart like pincers. Cheri's calligraphic script adds the cute, inviting flourish up top, and the plain sans below lets it stand out.
